Americans Buy a Fifth of China's Exports
I recently went to the gym and the 45 pound bench weights said "Made in China." That implies its cheaper to make and ship dead weight from China rather than make it here. Sad.

Yet we keep trying to lower/remove tariffs on imports from many countries, making it even cheaper to export the manufacturing of goods to countries like Burma and Cambodia where it is perfectly legal to employ children and treat them as little more than livestock, working them 14 hours a day for pennies.

It's not like those manufacturing jobs could be useful here or anything either.

That's not really so surprising. I could imagine that the USA buys a fifth of the world's products if you had to average everything out. It's a huge country and a huge population and much of the world's wealth is there. Perhaps if you counted all of Europe together they might also buy a fifth of China's exports. And even then it wouldn't be as large a country as the USA.
That's great. Or sad. Depending how you look at it.

Latex vs oil (note: the video doesn't explain the differences as well as the article)

I actually embarked on this very question. I always knew you should use oil for heavy based furniture, but in my experimentation, due to cost I was forced to go with a mix of latex and oil (spray) paints. I was warned it would be problematic, but as long as everything set before proceeding I shouldn't run into trouble.

One thing this article does not mention is a clear coat over latex! You can have all the benefits of latex, (such as price!) so long as you let it cure and then apply a heavy clear coat!
